label: map_1
name: Experimenting Causal Program Library
mech: The system keeps a growing library of small probabilistic programs, each encoding a candidate causal mechanism (e.g., "pressure causes leak if seal is worn"). When several programs explain the observations equally well, it computes which intervention (real action, simulator query or tool call) would best tell them apart, runs it, and reweights or deletes programs based on the result. New programs are synthesized by recombining fragments of programs that survived, so the library compresses over time.
value: It can discover and reliably use real cause-and-effect structure, including in situations that never appeared in its data.

label: map_1
name: Self-Revising Provenance Belief Ledger
mech: Every assertion the system adopts becomes a node in a persistent graph that stores its source, confidence and the nodes it was derived from. On each inference step a constraint checker scans for contradictions. Conflicts are resolved by retracting the least-supported justification, and the retraction automatically propagates to all dependent conclusions (truth maintenance). Generation is restricted to drawing on the active ledger and has to cite node IDs.
value: It enables lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting, with traceable reasoning and instant correction of any fact and everything derived from it.

label: map_1
name: Information-Priced Compute Market
mech: Many heterogeneous modules (search, simulation, symbolic solvers, small neural nets) bid for slices of a shared compute budget. A bid is priced by the expected reduction in task uncertainty, and the payout is the realized reduction. Modules that bid well gain budget and get copied with mutations, while chronically bad bidders are retired. The architecture is therefore an evolving economy rather than a fixed graph.
value: It makes possible adaptive, open-ended allocation of reasoning effort and self-directed architectural growth after deployment.

label: map_2
name: Audited Sleep Consolidation
mech: Surprising experiences go verbatim into a fast episodic buffer. During offline phases the system replays them to propose weight deltas inside a sandboxed copy of its slow network. Each delta is accepted only if a self-maintained regression suite of past skills shows no loss, and rejected deltas are stored as interference records that shape later proposals.
value: It enables continual lifelong learning after deployment without catastrophic forgetting.

label: map_2
name: Evolving Executable World Simulators
mech: The system maintains a population of small probabilistic programs, each a candidate simulator of some part of the environment. Queries are answered by running or intervening on the best-scoring simulators. Prediction errors drive program-synthesis mutations, and simulators are selected by how well they compress observations and predict accurately.
value: It gives explicit causal and counterfactual reasoning and lets the system discover new models that can be inspected.

label: map_2
name: Verified Competence Cartography
mech: An embedding-indexed map stores the system's ground-truth-verified error statistics for each region of problem space, updated whenever an outcome is checked. Before answering, the system looks up the query's region. It then answers, abstains, asks for information, or routes the region to the learning loop, depending on the measured reliability and the cost of being wrong.
value: It gives reliable self-knowledge of where the system is competent, so it can abstain and direct its own learning based on its actual track record.

label: map_3
name: Surprise-Gated Synaptic Patch Memory
mech: When prediction error on an input crosses a learned threshold, the system writes a small key-value module next to the frozen core. The key is the context embedding and the value is a low-rank change to the core's weights. Those changes take effect only when a later context is similar to that key. During an offline phase, the system replays old episodes against the patches. It merges patches that do the same thing and deletes ones that conflict, using how often they agree as the score. Each patch keeps a count of how often it was used and how often it was confirmed, and patches that stop earning their place are removed.
value: The system could learn permanently from a single experience without forgetting what it already knows or needing retraining.

label: map_3
name: Falsifiable Causal World-Graph
mech: Perception updates a running graph of objects, their attributes and typed causal links. Each link carries a probability and a count of how many times its predictions came true. Before each step the system simulates what it expects to observe, then compares that with what it actually observes. When they differ, it traces the error back through the graph to the links most to blame and revises them: it adds hidden variables, splits links or reverses their direction. It can also run interventions inside the graph to test competing explanations before acting.
value: The system could know when its beliefs are wrong, reason about counterfactuals, and keep a consistent, inspectable model of the world over long periods.

label: map_3
name: Verifier-Halted Constraint Relaxation
mech: A query is turned into a set of variables, which are partial answers and sub-goals, plus constraints between them that are learned or extracted from the query. Local update rules pass messages between these units, and the system keeps iterating until either a symbolic checker or a learned checker confirms that every constraint is met, or the energy of the system stops falling. When progress stalls, the system adds intermediate variables, for example lemmas or sub-plans, and stores successful arrangements as reusable templates.
value: The system could spend compute in proportion to how hard a problem is and solve multi-step problems it cannot solve in one pass, with a clear signal for when it has succeeded and when it has failed.

label: v15:g1_neg
name: Learned Dimensional Analysis Types
mech: Every internal quantity carries a vector of integer exponents over learned base "dimensions", like units in physics. Operations that mix incompatible dimensions are masked out. When data forces an inconsistent assignment, the system solves the integer linear system (Smith normal form) and adds a new base dimension. Predictions are made only through dimensionless groups found automatically, in the style of the Buckingham-pi theorem.
value: Built-in sanity checks and principled extrapolation far outside the training range, because laws written in dimensionless form transfer across scales.

label: v15:g1_neg
name: Reversible Core, Ancilla Tape
mech: Every layer is a bijection, and any information a step would normally discard is written exactly to an ancilla tape. The tape's length measures how much was forgotten. Abduction runs the network backward: fix the desired output, edit the ancilla, and recover exactly which inputs would produce it. Unlearning removes one example's influence by un-computing its trace.
value: Exact provenance, exact counterfactual inputs ("what would have had to be true?") and certified forgetting, none of which LLMs can do because they discard information at every layer.

label: v15:g1_neg
name: Entrained Oscillator Time Sense
mech: A bank of coupled phase oscillators (Kuramoto dynamics) runs continuously, and timestamped events phase-reset or nudge them. Concepts and routines are stored as stable phase-locking patterns between oscillators, not as static vectors. Each oscillator adapts its natural frequency to minimize phase error at event onsets, and an expectation is read out as the phase at which the next event should arrive.
value: A real sense of duration, rhythm, deadlines and "something is late", including discovering hidden periodicities in event streams. Token-sequence models have no clock, so they cannot do this.

label: v15:g1_core
name: Kinetic Proofreading Reasoning Cascade
mech: Each candidate reasoning step gets a "binding margin": how strongly it is re-derived when the context is re-encoded in a different way. The step then passes n sequential stages, and at each stage the context decorrelates further (paraphrase, dropout, abstraction). The chance of being discarded rises as the margin falls, and a discarded step cannot be restored. Only steps that survive all n stages are committed, so the error rate falls roughly as ε^n. The system adapts n, the compute it spends, to how much downstream work depends on the step.
value: Long chains can be made as reliable as needed, with an explicit dial between speed and accuracy, instead of errors compounding.

label: v15:g1_core
name: Duplication-Degeneration Skill Growth
mech: Each module stores a compact functional signature: its input-output behavior on a probe set. When the gradient from new data conflicts with that signature beyond a threshold, the module is duplicated rather than overwritten. Both copies then receive complementary sparse degeneration masks, so each loses a different subset of sub-functions while the pair together still reproduces the old signature. The new copy specializes on the new data. Copies that end up redundant are pruned.
value: New capabilities can grow after deployment, with old ones preserved in the network's structure rather than by penalties or replay.

label: v15:g1_core
name: Lock-In Concept Extraction
mech: To learn a new concept from a few examples, the system modulates the hypothesized feature (present or absent, at varying strength) across its inputs following a pseudo-random reference code. Per-channel integrators multiply each internal activation by the reference and low-pass the product, which pulls out the channels coherently locked to the concept even far below the noise. The locked channel set becomes a durable address for the concept. A new code then re-tests the address, and channels whose lock fades are dropped.
value: Concepts can be isolated precisely from very few, noisy examples, with a signal-to-noise level that can be measured.

label: v15:g1_core2
name: Assimilated Knowledge Ensemble
mech: The system keeps about 64 copies of a "knowledge state", which is a subset of its parameters. Each new fact or correction is handled as a weather-style observation. The update gain comes from the copies' cross-covariance between parameters and their predictions of that fact. A learned taper limits the update to parameters close to the fact in concept space, which stops a new fact from overwriting distant ones. When the copies agree too much, they are spread apart again so the system can keep learning.
value: The system can absorb a stream of new facts and corrections, each with a real confidence level, without retraining, and without the long-range damage that causes forgetting.

label: v15:g1_core2
name: Survey-Adjusted Reasoning Networks
mech: Each intermediate claim is a "station" that is derived along at least two independent routes, so the routes form closed loops. Each loop has a computed mismatch (misclosure). A least-squares adjustment spreads small mismatches across the loop, and Baarda's w-test singles out the one derivation step that is a blunder. Each claim gets a redundancy number. Any claim with a value near zero is unchecked, so the planner deliberately adds a new route to it before answering.
value: Long chains of reasoning check themselves. The system can say which step is wrong and which conclusions nothing has verified yet.

label: v15:g1_core2
name: Capture-Recapture Ignorance Estimator
mech: For a given query, the system runs several retrieval or generation passes that are deliberately independent, each using different cues, sources or decompositions. It records which candidate facts or solutions each pass "captures". From the overlaps it computes Chao or Lincoln-Petersen estimates of how many relevant items are still missing, adjusting for the fact that some items are easier to capture than others. It keeps sampling until the estimated unseen share falls below a set threshold, and its answer states how complete it is.
value: The system can say "I have probably found 90% of the relevant cases" and know when to stop searching.

label: v15:g1_mech
name: Dimensional Exponent Tagging
mech: Every internal quantity carries, alongside its real-valued vector, a short integer vector of exponents over a learned set of base "kinds" (like length, time, count, agent). When two quantities are multiplied or divided, their exponent vectors add or subtract. When they are added or compared, the exponents must match, and any mismatch produces an imbalance residual. That residual is the learning signal. Persistent mismatches over many examples cause a new base kind or a conversion constant to be created, and kinds that never constrain anything are merged away.
value: Reasoning steps that make no physical or logical sense get rejected because their kinds don't match, and the system can extrapolate to unseen magnitudes by scaling rules instead of memorized examples.

label: v15:g1_mech
name: Double-Entry Conservation Ledger
mech: Each state change described in the input or produced during reasoning is written as a transfer: one amount debited from one holder and credited to another, across a learned set of conserved quantities (objects, money, people, information). After every step, the totals for each quantity are summed, and they must balance. A nonzero imbalance is the training signal. If the imbalance persists, the system creates a new hidden holder to absorb it and keeps that holder only if it later balances other transfers. Quantities whose totals never actually stay constant get demoted from the conserved set.
value: The system can track the state of the world exactly over very long sequences, and it can infer unmentioned participants or leaks from bookkeeping gaps.

label: v15:g1_mech
name: Self-Discovered Symmetry Harvesting
mech: The system keeps a growing pool of candidate input transformations, built by composing primitive edits: relabel, permute, reflect, rescale, swap roles. At inference it answers both the original input and several transformed copies, maps each answer back through the inverse transformation, and measures how much the answers disagree. A transformation's score rises when answers agree on cases that were verified correct, and it falls when they diverge. High-scoring transformations are kept and used both to vote at inference and to enlarge the training data. Low scorers are discarded, and recombinations of kept ones are proposed as new candidates.
value: The system finds on its own which changes to an input must not change the answer, which gives it structured generalization far outside its training distribution.

label: v15:g1_loop
name: Rigidity-Counted Concept Frameworks
mech: Concepts are stored as points in an embedding space, and each learned fact is a constraint between points (distance, angle or relation). The system keeps computing the rigidity matrix of this framework. Its null space gives "floppy modes", directions in which a concept can move without breaking any known fact, so the concept is underdetermined. Each floppy mode creates a bracing latent variable or a targeted query along that direction. Each state of self-stress (constraints that are redundant and in conflict) splits the stressed concept into two nodes, so that each one meets a consistent subset of the constraints.
value: The system can tell, from the geometry alone, exactly which parts of its knowledge are underdetermined or overconstrained, and it repairs each part structurally.

label: v15:g1_loop
name: Wahlund Splitting of Representations
mech: Each internal unit's discretized activation states are treated as alleles, and pairs of co-occurring contexts are treated as diploid genotypes. A running Hardy–Weinberg test compares how often mixed ("heterozygous") pairs actually occur with how often they would occur in one homogeneous population. A significant heterozygote deficit is the Wahlund signature that the unit merges hidden subpopulations. In that case the unit is split into typed children, and the F-statistics between those children decide the routing. Children that later come back into equilibrium with each other are merged again.
value: The model breaks apart conflated concepts while it runs, using an online statistical test instead of an analysis done after the fact.

label: v15:g1_loop
name: Misclosure-Driven Context Charts
mech: Learned transformations (analogies, translations, coordinate maps) are composed around closed cycles, and each cycle's misclosure is recorded the way a surveyor records a traverse error. A Hodge decomposition of these residuals over the cycle complex leads to three repairs. The gradient part goes back into local map corrections. The curl part localizes and deletes or rewires the specific inconsistent edges. The harmonic part shows a real topological hole, and it creates a new context variable that divides the domain into separate charts with explicit transition maps.
value: The system can find out that its knowledge needs several context-dependent frames, and build them, instead of averaging contradictory regularities into one incoherent map.

label: v15:g2_imm
name: Schild-Slope Feature Splitting
mech: For pairs of cues that compete over an internal feature, the system measures dose-response shifts, meaning how much more of cue A is needed as cue B increases, and fits a Schild slope. A slope of 1 confirms that one mechanism mediates both cues. If the slope differs from 1, the feature is split into two sites, each with its own learned gate. The slopes are stored per feature, and they are re-tested whenever new competing cues show up. First test: In a toy model with planted features (some single-mechanism, some secretly two superposed mechanisms), titrate competing cue pairs and fit Schild slopes on feature activation; success is ≥85% correct single-versus-composite classification (single-mechanism slopes within 0.9–1.1) and better causal-ablation faithfulness after splitting.
value: Features that are secretly several mechanisms get found and separated by a quantitative invariant, so the model's internals become more faithful and reasoning that combines cues becomes more reliable.

label: v15:g2_imm
name: Complementation-Group Remodularization
mech: When a behavior fails, the system creates small parameter lesions that reproduce the failure. Pairs of lesions are "crossed" by mixing activations from the two lesioned copies. If the mix restores the behavior, the lesions sit in different functional units. If it doesn't, they sit in the same one. The groups found this way define module boundaries, and parameters are re-partitioned and re-routed to match. A map of the groups is stored and updated as new failures appear. First test: On a small transformer trained with planted, block-sparse modules for four synthetic subtasks, generate failure-reproducing lesions, cross pairs via activation mixing, and cluster; success is adjusted Rand index ≥0.7 against planted modules, exceeding activation-correlation clustering.
value: The module structure comes from functional evidence, not from a design chosen in advance, so fixes, transfer and growth stay local to the unit that is actually responsible.

label: v15:g2_imm
name: Four-Point Reticulate Concept Hierarchy
mech: The system continuously runs the four-point condition on embedding distances among concepts in its taxonomy. Quartets that violate it point to hybrid concepts, and those concepts are re-typed as reticulation nodes with two weighted parent lineages. Properties are then inherited from both parents. The violation magnitudes are stored, and edges are reweighted as evidence accumulates. First test: Using WordNet/Wiktionary-etymology concepts with ~200 labeled hybrids (loanword blends, hybrid species, fusion genres) and matched non-hybrids, compute four-point-condition violations on off-the-shelf embedding distances; success is AUROC ≥0.75 for flagging hybrids and higher property-prediction accuracy than single-parent tree inheritance.
value: The system can represent and reason about concepts that blend lineages, such as loanwords, hybrid organisms or mixed genres, which strictly tree-shaped hierarchies get wrong.

label: v15:g2_evo1
name: Hole-Filling Derivation Probes
mech: Claims are nodes, and derivations are edges that carry transformations; whatever error is left after going round a loop is that loop's misclosure. When the Hodge split finds a harmonic residual, the system doesn't accept it as a real gap straight away. First it builds bridging derivations across the gap, choosing them with Baarda's minimal-detectable-bias so that each new derivation best tells the possible explanations apart. If the new pieces bring the error back to zero, it was a mistake, and the w-test finds the bad step. If the error survives every bridge, the system creates a new context variable that splits the claims into separate frames. First test: Build 300 synthetic claim graphs of unit-conversion derivations whose loops misclose either from one injected wrong step or from a hidden two-frame split (two exchange-rate regimes); success is ≥85% correct mistake-versus-frame verdicts with correct step localization, beating treating every harmonic residual as a gap.
value: The system can tell a mistake in its own reasoning apart from a real need for separate frames, and it finds out by running its own test.

label: v15:g2_evo1
name: Stress-Space Bookkeeping
mech: Holders are learned points, and each transfer is a bar between two of them. A balanced set of transfers is an equilibrium stress, so a quantity counts as conserved only while its transfers stay in that stress space. An imbalance that won't go away is treated as a load on the framework. The system adds a hidden holder at the position where the loose directions (floppy modes) can absorb that load. Where stresses conflict, the holder splits in two. First test: On synthetic ledger worlds with 10–30 holders where 1–3 holders are removed from the transfer log, fit the bar-framework stress model; success is ≥80% recovery of hidden-holder count and their transfer partners, beating a per-holder imbalance-threshold baseline.
value: The system can keep exact track of world state, and the geometry shows where unknown participants must be and which quantities are not really conserved.

label: v15:g2_evo1
name: Delayed Proofreading Assimilation
mech: A new fact first goes into a queue. At each stage it is checked against a different, separate subset of the roughly 64 ensemble members, and only after other facts have been absorbed in between. Agreement between those members gives the fact's binding margin, and a fact rejected at any stage is gone for good. The number of stages grows with how much of the model the update would change. Facts that pass more stages get smaller observation noise, so the update counts them more. First test: Stream 1,000 factual updates (half correct, half deliberately false with broad downstream reach) from zsRE into a 64-member LoRA ensemble with staged disjoint-subset gating; success is ≥80% false-fact rejection at ≥90% true-fact acceptance, beating single-stage ensemble voting on neighborhood accuracy.
value: The system can keep learning from a stream of new facts, and wrong facts that would cause broad damage are stopped before they get in.

label: v15:g2_evo2
name: Self-Calibrating Ledger Adjustment
mech: Every double-entry balance identity is treated as a surveying condition equation. A least-squares adjustment runs over all transfers, and Baarda w-tests compare two kinds of explanation: "a blunder in step k" (a residual pattern local to one step) and "an unseen holder h" (one systematic pattern shared across many balance loops). Hidden holders are added the way self-calibration adds parameters: only when they pass a significance test and lower the minimal detectable bias of other claims. Variance-component estimation learns a reliability weight for each quantity, which continuously demotes a quantity toward "approximately conserved". Redundancy numbers point the planner to the claims nothing checks yet, and it then asks for or derives the one extra count that would close a loop around them. First test: Generate 500 synthetic multi-step transfer stories (bAbI-style ledgers) with one injected arithmetic blunder or one omitted holder each; run the adjustment with w-tests; success is ≥85% correct blunder-versus-holder classification and step localization, beating a largest-residual baseline by ≥15 points.
value: The system can track world state over very long texts and say which step is wrong or which unmentioned participant must exist, with a stated confidence in each verdict.

label: v15:g2_evo2
name: Hodge-Sorted Chart Proofreading
mech: Each proofreading stage re-encodes the context with a learned map (paraphrase, abstraction, dropout). A step's binding margins across these encodings therefore form edge flows on a cycle complex, and a Hodge decomposition splits them into three parts. The gradient part is encoder bias: correct the map and keep the step. The curl part is real fragility: discard the step irreversibly. The harmonic part means the step holds only in some contexts: commit it locally to a new chart, with an explicit context variable and a transition map. Later steps that cross chart boundaries face extra proofreading stages, scaled to the misclosure of the transition map they cross. A new chart is kept only if steps committed in it survive this proofreading. First test: On 500 GSM8K chains plus 200 synthetic problems whose steps hold only under one of two stated rule sets, score steps under four re-encodings and Hodge-split the margins; success is lower final-answer error than majority-vote proofreading while retaining ≥90% of context-conditional true steps.
value: Error rates in long reasoning drop exponentially without discarding conclusions that are true only in some contexts, and the system learns where its knowledge splits into separate frames.

label: v17:g1_neg
name: Time-Sealed Commitment Escrow
mech: The system turns each belief into a falsifiable prediction about future raw data streams, such as sensor feeds, registries, prices or archives. It hash-commits the prediction together with a resolver: a small, deterministic parsing predicate frozen at commit time. Weights may learn only from predictions that have matured, and each one is scored by its frozen resolver against data that did not exist when the model made the claim. The escrow ledger stores calibration per domain and per horizon, and resolvers that drift or turn out ambiguous are retired.
value: The current model cannot shape its own grade, because the world settles the score later through a judge fixed before the outcome existed.

label: v17:g1_neg
name: Triangulated Independent-View Accuracy
mech: Three or more predictor lineages are trained on disjoint evidence channels about the same events, such as text reports, numeric logs and imagery. The channels are chosen so that their errors are conditionally independent. From the pairwise and three-way rates at which the lineages agree, a latent-class (Dawid-Skene-style) estimator recovers each lineage's accuracy per region without any labels. The system trains only on events where the triangulated posterior is confident. It runs higher-order agreement tests to detect when independence has broken down and then splits or reroutes channels.
value: It gives label-free, mathematically identifiable accuracy estimates in open domains, derived from how independent views agree rather than from any one model judging itself.

label: v17:g1_neg
name: Planted-Canary Capture-Recapture
mech: The system corrupts known-true items to create canary errors whose falsehood it knows by construction, and mixes them into its normal stream of claims. Two error-detection procedures with different mechanisms flag suspect claims. Their catch rates on canaries measure each procedure's recall. The overlap of their real-error catches, combined with that recall, gives a Lincoln-Petersen estimate of how many errors went undetected in each domain. The canary generator adapts its corruptions so that, statistically, canaries cannot be told apart from the real errors detected so far. Learning budget goes to domains whose estimated hidden-error mass is largest.
value: The system can measure the errors it has not caught, using ground truth it planted itself, instead of trusting its own sense of being right.

label: v17:g1_core
name: Survey-Adjusted Belief Network
mech: Every quantitative or relational claim the system holds is treated as a surveyed observation with a variance, and it is linked to independent observations (retrieved sources, tool outputs, sensor readings) through closed constraint loops. Weighted least-squares adjustment spreads each loop's misclosure across its claims. Baarda's normalized-residual test then names the specific claim that is most likely a blunder, which gets revised or discarded. For each claim the system stores a redundancy number that says how far other observations control it. Claims with near-zero redundancy are marked as structurally unverifiable rather than as trusted.
value: The system can locate and fix its own errors, and knows which beliefs nothing can currently check, without an oracle or a self-grading model.

label: v17:g1_core
name: Innovation-Diagnosed Continual Assimilation
mech: The model's beliefs act as a background state. Each new datum from a document, user, instrument or tool is an observation, and the system computes the innovation (observation minus prediction) and the analysis residual. Desroziers consistency identities over these statistics give separate estimates of the model's error covariance and of each source's error covariance, so no labels are needed. These estimates set the gain that decides how much each observation changes the stored beliefs and parameters. A source whose estimated error grows is down-weighted automatically, and so is a model region whose estimated error grows.
value: The system learns continuously from noisy, adversarial real-world streams while measuring its own reliability and each source's reliability from the data alone.

label: v17:g1_core
name: Extrinsic-Exchange Turbo Reasoning
mech: A problem is decomposed in two deliberately different orders (an interleaver). This produces two reasoning chains whose intermediate claims are scored as log-likelihood ratios against parity-like constraints (units, conservation laws, cited values). On each pass, a chain subtracts the belief it received from the other chain before sending its own update. Only extrinsic evidence crosses over, so neither chain counts its own conclusions twice. Mutual-information transfer (EXIT) curves are stored per problem type. They predict whether the exchange will converge, and when it will not, the answer is withheld and the system goes looking for more constraints.
value: Long reasoning chains can correct each other without an echo chamber, and the system can tell beforehand when internal checking cannot reach a reliable answer.

label: v17:g1_loop
name: Reconciliation-Driven Derivation Pruning
mech: Every quantity or claim the system asserts is computed along several derivation paths that share no sources, linked by arithmetic, unit and accounting identities. Weighted least squares adjusts the estimates so the identities hold, a chi-square test checks how far they fail to close, and a per-path test isolates the path most likely to carry a gross error. That path is retired, given a learned bias term, or split by context where its errors cluster. Agreement between independent paths under fixed identities is the correctness signal, so no oracle or self-judgment is needed.

label: v17:g1_loop
name: Capture-Recapture Blind-Spot Growth
mech: Several critics trained on disjoint views of the data flag suspected errors in the system's outputs. A latent-class capture-recapture model fits the overlaps between their flags and estimates each critic's false-flag rate, how strongly the critics depend on each other, and how many errors went uncaught in each input region. Where the estimated uncaught errors are high, the system trains a new critic on a fresh disjoint view. Where critics have become too similar, it retrains one of them to make them independent again, and it deletes critics whose catches the others already cover.
value: The system can measure what it fails to notice and grow detectors exactly there, without an oracle.

label: v17:g1_loop
name: Standard-Addition Matrix Calibration
mech: The system injects graded perturbations into live tasks, and the correct effect of each one is known by construction: inserted facts with fixed consequences, unit rescalings, swapped entities, planted sub-results. It fits a line of output shift against spike size. The slope gives recovery for that input type, and extrapolating the line to zero spike gives a bias-corrected answer. Input types with low or uneven recovery get their own adapter modules, and an adapter is deleted if recovery does not improve. The system only grades known differences, never its own absolute answers.

label: v17:g1_mech
name: Sealed Forecasts Against Time
mech: Whenever the system makes a claim, it also writes down concrete, checkable predictions about data that has not arrived yet: future entries in incoming streams, logs, measurements or published records that the system cannot write to. Each prediction is stored with a fingerprint and a deadline so it cannot be changed afterwards. When the data arrives, a fixed string or number comparison settles the prediction mechanically. Only settled predictions change the parameters, and each update is weighted by how surprising the outcome was. The claims that produced wrong forecasts lose influence on future answers.
value: The system can correct itself in open-ended domains with no oracle, because the world's future acts as the grader and that grader cannot be flattered or influenced.

label: v17:g1_mech
name: Disjoint-Evidence Agreement Ledger
mech: The raw evidence is split into partitions that do not overlap, and a separate copy of the system is trained on each one. The copies answer the same question independently. Agreement counts as a label only when the copies' evidence is disjoint. Its weight shrinks by how correlated their errors are, which is measured by quietly corrupting one partition and seeing whether the other copies follow the corruption. A ledger stores, for each pair of copies, how often they agree by chance and how often their errors move together. Copies whose dissent later turns out justified get more weight.

label: v17:g1_mech
name: Known-Effect Transformation Audits
mech: A small rule set, checked once by hand, holds transformations whose effect on the correct answer is fixed by construction. Examples: swapping units should rescale a number, reordering items should leave a count unchanged, duplicating a list should double a sum, and negating a premise should flip a conclusion. The system answers both the original question and its transformed version. Any answer pair that breaks the known relationship is certainly wrong, whatever the true answer is. The violation rate is stored for each pair of topic and transformation, and the parameters are pushed toward restoring the relationship. Topics with high violation rates get the most new transformations.
value: The system finds certain errors on questions nobody knows the answer to, because the error signal comes from fixed algebra rather than from the model's opinion.

label: v17:g1_genius
name: Walk-Forward Self-Backtesting
mech: The system keeps snapshot copies of itself, each trained only on data before a strict cutoff date, and asks them questions that the archive settled after that date. The archive grades their answers with no model judgment involved. The system stores which reasoning strategies and update rules improved these later-verified answers and transfers only those to the present model. Contamination audits drop any snapshot whose training data leaked material from after its cutoff.
value: It turns the passage of time into an oracle for open-ended domains, so improvement is graded by the world rather than by the model itself.

label: v17:g1_genius
name: Metamorphic-Relation Correctness Oracle
mech: The system keeps a growing library of input transformations, each paired with a relation its outputs must provably satisfy: unit changes rescale answers, irrelevant permutations leave them unchanged, and counterfactual edits move them in a known direction. Each answer is re-asked under these transformations, and violations of the relations are the training loss. New relations are kept only if they are derivable a priori, for example from symmetry, dimensional analysis or the structure of the edit.
value: It detects and corrects errors without ever knowing the true answer, as metamorphic testing does for programs that have no test oracle.

label: v17:g1_genius
name: Teachability-Graded Claims
mech: Each claim or explanation the system produces is given to a small, freshly initialized student model. The claim is scored by how much it improves the student's prediction of held-out raw observations from the domain, compared with a student that did not receive it. The system stores these gains per claim and trains itself toward claims with high gains, while claims with no gain are demoted.

label: v17:g2_evo1
name: Claim-Versus-Negation Edit Contrast
mech: For each claim, the system makes two small weight edits: one that asserts the claim and one that asserts its negation. The difference in log-likelihood, compared against a null distribution from edits of random claims, is stored as the claim's support. Claims the world prefers are consolidated, and claims whose negation predicts better are retracted. Claims that sit inside the null band are labelled "uncontrolled by any data" rather than trusted. label: v17:g2_evo1
name: Predictable-Surprise Gain Correction
mech: The system logs its surprise (log-loss) on every incoming datum, tagged by source and knowledge region. It continuously regresses each region's later surprise on earlier surprises from each source. A positive lagged correlation means that source was under-weighted; a negative one, where the model was misled and corrected later, means it was over-weighted. These coefficients directly set the per-source trust weights and per-region learning rates, which are adjusted until the surprise sequences become unpredictable. label: v17:g2_evo1
name: Sealed Pre-Lookup Wagers

label: v17:g2_evo2
name: Restoring-Force Belief Sounding

A slope near zero marks the region as uncheckable. A real belief that deviates from its neighbour-implied value by more than the measured slope allows is flagged as a likely blunder and revised. Regions whose slope drops trigger targeted relearning, and the slope is measured again afterwards. label: v17:g2_evo2
name: Leave-Out Forecast Credit

label: v17:g2_imm
name: Depth-Asymmetry Truth Serum

label: v17:g2_imm
name: Stemmatic Error Genealogy

A claim counts as corroborated only when it appears in branches that the tree shows to be independent; support from copies of one ancestor counts once. label: v17:g2_imm
name: Recapture Census of Errors

label: v15V:v15:g2_evo1
name: Hodge-Audited Claim Graph
mech: Claims are nodes and derivations are transformation edges. A Hodge decomposition splits the misclosure of every loop into three parts: a curl part (local, so the faulty step can be found with a w-test), a harmonic part (global, so it is either a mistake or a real frame split), and a gradient part (systematic offsets that no loop can see). The harmonic part gets bridging derivations, each chosen by minimal-detectable-bias and taken from a different source than the loop it crosses (tool, retrieval, model). If the misclosure collapses, it was a mistake. If it survives every bridge, a context variable splits the frames. The crux is handled by the decomposition itself: the gradient subspace is exactly what the system cannot grade by itself, so the system never trusts it and spends external observations ("control points") only on the nodes that span it.
value: The system can find and classify its own reasoning errors with no oracle, and it can say exactly which beliefs only outside evidence can check.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core2
name: Self-Calibrating Knowledge Assimilation
mech: About 64 ensemble copies of a parameter subset take each new fact as an observation, with a gain built from parameter-prediction cross-covariance and a learned locality taper so that distant knowledge is untouched. Before a fact is assimilated, it is used as an honest forecast test: its innovation (observed minus ensemble-predicted) is compared against the ensemble spread plus that source's error variance. Desroziers-style innovation statistics, gathered over many facts, estimate each source's error variance online, so unreliable sources are down-weighted automatically, and a fact that fails the chi-square gate is quarantined instead of written in. The correctness signal therefore comes from prequential consistency between independent future observations and prior forecasts, not from the model judging itself.
value: The system can keep absorbing streams of facts and corrections from sources of unknown reliability, learning how far to trust each one, without retraining and without forgetting.

label: v15V:v15:g1_mech
name: Falsifiable Learned Kind Algebra
mech: Every internal quantity carries an integer exponent vector over learned base kinds. Multiplication adds the vectors, and addition or comparison requires them to match, so an imbalance is computed by exact integer arithmetic, not by a learned judge. The model only proposes kind assignments. These are scored against expressions people actually write in corpora, tables and spreadsheets (external data the model did not produce), and the score maximizes the number of syntactically possible combinations the kind system forbids while keeping zero imbalance on observed expressions. This stops the trivial "everything is one kind" solution. A persistent imbalance creates a new kind or a conversion constant, and a kind that forbids nothing is merged away.
value: Nonsensical reasoning steps are rejected by an exact check that the fallible model cannot argue its way around, and magnitudes extrapolate through scaling rules.

label: v15V:v15:g1_neg
name: Cross-Scale Dimensionless Predictor
mech: Quantities carry integer dimension exponents, and Smith normal form over them yields the dimensionless groups. Every prediction is a learned function of those groups only. The correctness signal is cross-scale transfer on real data: a pi-law fitted on one magnitude band must predict observations in another band unchanged, because the world, not the model, supplies the variation in scale. If transfer fails while the in-band fit holds, the dimension assignment is wrong. SNF then adds a base dimension that separates the offending groups, and the scale test is re-run.
value: The system can extrapolate far outside its training range, with a built-in falsification test whenever its notion of "same kind of quantity" is wrong.

label: v15V:v15:g2_evo2
name: Geodetic Adjustment of World-State
anchor: Ledger balances as surveying condition equations
mech: Every conservation identity in a narrative ledger becomes a condition equation in a least-squares adjustment. Baarda w-tests then decide between "blunder at step k" (a local residual) and "hidden holder h" (a shared pattern across loops), and a holder is admitted only if it passes significance and lowers other claims' minimal detectable bias. The conservation identities act as the oracle because they are structural, not judged by the model. Variance-component estimation learns per quantity how strictly conservation actually holds. Redundancy numbers mark the claims that no identity checks, and only for those does the planner request or derive one extra external count.
value: The system can track world state over very long texts, saying which step is wrong or which unmentioned participant must exist, with a confidence for each verdict and an explicit list of what it cannot check.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core
name: Exclusive-Pair Calibrated Commit Cascade
mech: Each candidate step passes n stages of increasingly decorrelated re-encoding, and it is discarded irreversibly with a probability that rises as its binding margin falls. The true per-stage false-pass rate is measured without an oracle by also pushing mutually exclusive step pairs through the cascade (the step and a sampled contradicting alternative). At most one of each pair can be true, so the fraction where both survive gives a lower bound on false-pass. Comparing that fraction stage by stage exposes correlated stages, which are replaced with more distant re-encodings. n is then set from the measured rate, not the assumed ε^n, and scaled by how much downstream work depends on the step.
value: Long reasoning chains get a calibrated, self-measured reliability dial instead of compounding errors or overconfident self-verification.

label: v15V:v15:g1_loop
name: Rigidity-Braced Concept Framework
mech: Concepts are points and facts are geometric constraints, and the system continuously computes the framework's rigidity matrix. Its null space (floppy modes) marks underdetermined concepts, which trigger a query along exactly that direction, and an answer is accepted only if it removes the mode without creating stress. A state of self-stress is the oracle-free error signal. If the stress concentrates on one constraint, that fact is retracted. If it splits the constraints into two groups that are each rigid and stress-free, the concept is split in two. Facts in redundant, stress-free regions are trusted because they are cross-checked; facts in floppy regions are explicitly unverified.
value: From geometry alone, the system can tell where its knowledge is wrong, ambiguous or unverified, and repair each case structurally.

label: v15V:v15:g2_imm
name: Complementation-Mapped Modular Network
mech: Small parameter lesions that change a behavior are paired and "crossed" by mixing activations between the two lesioned copies. Restoration means separate functional units and no restoration means the same unit, and the resulting groups re-partition and re-route the parameters. The reference phenotype is the intact model's own output, not a correct answer, so module discovery needs no oracle. A proposed fix for an externally flagged failure is accepted only if it complements the lesions of exactly one group and leaves behavior on the other groups' probes unchanged. The anchor cannot say what counts as a failure (that one flag stays external), but it makes localization and side-effect checking oracle-free.
value: The system's module structure comes from functional evidence, so fixes, transfer and growth stay local and their side effects can be verified.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core
name: World-Arbitrated Degenerate Twins
mech: When the gradient from new data conflicts with a module's frozen probe signature, the module splits into two twins. The twins get complementary sparse masks, so only the pair together reproduces the old signature, and the system judges between them only by which one better predicted the world's next observation. Because the pair holds the old signature by construction, neither twin can win by rewriting past behavior. They compete only on inputs where they disagree, and each disagreement is held as an open bet until the delayed outcome arrives (the next item in a stream, the result of an action, a later document). A twin's own sub-functions are pruned only after it loses bets it placed itself, so the correctness signal is always a prediction made before the outcome, never a judgment made afterward.
value: The system keeps learning new skills after deployment, with old skills preserved in its structure and new ones checked against what the world later shows, not by grading itself.

label: v15V:v15:g2_imm
name: Cross-Metric Reticulation Detector
mech: Four-point-condition violations among concept quartets are computed separately in several distance metrics, each built from independent evidence (text co-occurrence, shared properties, form or etymology, perception). A concept becomes a two-parent reticulation node only when all of the metrics show the violation and each one gives the same admixture weight. A real hybrid is overdetermined: its mixing proportion is one number that every independent geometry must reproduce. An artifact of one embedding breaks tree-additivity in that metric only, and the weight it gives disagrees with the others. Accepted nodes inherit properties from both parents in that proportion, and the weights are re-solved as new evidence arrives, so a node whose weights drift apart across metrics is demoted.
value: The system can represent concepts that blend lineages, such as loanwords, hybrid species and fusion genres, and can tell real hybrids from artifacts of its own embeddings without a labeled oracle.

label: v15V:v15:g1_loop
name: Wahlund-Certified Unit Splitting
mech: Each unit's discretized activation states are treated as alleles over pairs of co-occurring contexts. A heterozygote deficit relative to the Hardy–Weinberg expectation triggers a split into child units. The split is kept only if it satisfies the Wahlund identity on new context pairs: each child must return to Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium (F_IS near 0), and the variance in allele frequency between the children (F_ST) must account numerically for the parent's deficit. This tests the unit against a calibrated null model with known false-positive rates rather than judging the model's own outputs, so a spurious split leaves a deficit inside a child or an unexplained gap, and is merged back.
value: The model breaks apart conflated concepts while it runs, and every split is certified by a statistical identity checked on new data rather than by the model's own opinion of the result.

label: v15V:v15:g1_mech
name: Double-Entry World Ledger
mech: Every state change is posted as a debit from one holder and a credit to another, across a learned set of conserved quantities. Any nonzero sum after a step is the error signal, and it needs no oracle because balance is an algebraic invariant, not a judgment. To stop the system from balancing its books by invention, a hidden holder created to absorb a persistent imbalance must be issued as a forecast of which future transfers it will settle. It is removed if those transfers never arrive or if a total stated in the input (a count, a balance, a census) contradicts it. A quantity is dropped from the conserved set when stated totals for it repeatedly fail to reconcile.
value: The system can track world state exactly over very long sequences and infer unmentioned participants or leaks, and later input can disprove each such inference.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core2
name: Geodetic Reasoning Network Adjustment
anchor: loop misclosure adjustment with Baarda's w-test
mech: Each intermediate claim is a station derived along several routes. A least-squares adjustment with Baarda's w-test finds the faulty step in any loop that fails to close. Routes produced by the same model can share an error and still close perfectly, so the adjustment carries a covariance between routes, estimated from shared premises, sub-steps and tools. From that it computes, for every claim, its minimal detectable bias: the largest error that could still hide in that claim given those correlations. A claim whose minimal detectable bias is too large is not answered until the planner adds a new route to a control station, meaning a value fixed outside the model (a measurement, an executed computation, a cited source), just as a survey is anchored to fixed benchmarks.
value: Long reasoning chains find their own faulty step and state, for each conclusion, how large an error could still be undetected, instead of mistaking self-agreement for verification.

label: v15V:v15:g2_evo1
name: Rigidity Ledger with Floppy Modes
mech: Holders are points and transfers are bars between them. A quantity counts as conserved exactly when its observed transfers lie in the framework's equilibrium-stress space, which linear algebra checks without the model's judgment. A persistent imbalance is treated as a load. A hidden holder is placed where the floppy modes can carry that load, and Maxwell counting then fixes how many new bars it must have and to which holders, which predicts transfers not yet observed. The holder is kept only if later transfers fall on those predicted bars and the dimension of the stress space changes as counted. Where the predicted stresses conflict, the holder splits in two.
value: The system can keep exact track of world state and locate unseen participants, with their existence and connections derived from the framework's geometry and confirmed by later observations.

label: v15V:v15:g2_evo2
name: Hodge-Proofread Reasoning Charts
anchor: Hodge split of margins across re-encodings
mech: Each reasoning step is scored under several re-encodings of its context, drawn from different kinds of source (paraphrase, formal translation, a different model, a tool run). The margins are treated as edge flows on the graph of encodings and given a Hodge decomposition. The gradient part is a per-encoder bias, estimated across all steps and subtracted. The curl part is inconsistency, and the step is discarded. The harmonic part becomes a local chart with an explicit context variable. The decomposition is trusted only if, after fitting on k encodings, it predicts the step's margin on a new encoding before that encoding is scored. That held-out prediction is the correctness signal, so neither a biased encoder nor an overfit chart can certify itself. A chart whose transition maps keep mispredicting new encodings is dissolved.
value: Long reasoning becomes more reliable without throwing away conclusions that hold only in some contexts, and the system learns where its knowledge splits into separate frames.

label: v15V:v15:g1_neg
name: Reversible Network with Ancilla Audit
mech: Every layer is a bijection, and every bit a step would discard is written to an ancilla tape, so the network can run backward exactly. To check an output, the system fixes both the actual input and the output and runs backward. The number of ancilla bits that must be invented to reconcile the two is an exact bit count of how much of the output the input does not support, not the model's opinion of it. Zero invented bits means the output follows from its evidence, a high count means it was fabricated, and that count is the training signal. One example's influence is removed by uncomputing its trace. The audit separates grounded content from invented content, but it does not certify that the input itself is true.
value: The system gets exact provenance, a measured count of unsupported information in every claim, exact counterfactual inputs and certified forgetting, none of which an LLM can provide because it discards information at every layer.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core2
name: Capture-Recapture Self-Census
mech: Several retrieval or generation passes, built to fail in different ways (different sources, cues and decompositions), each "capture" candidate items, and every item gets a capture history: the set of passes that found it. A latent-class log-linear capture-recapture model fitted to these histories does two things. It estimates how many real items are still unseen, and it separates real items, which independent passes recapture, from phantoms, which stay confined to one pass or one correlated group of passes. The pass-interaction terms show where passes share a bias, and the system then adds a pass that breaks that dependence. Sampling stops when both the estimated unseen share and the estimated phantom share fall below a threshold.
value: Without any oracle, the system can say both "I have probably found 90% of the relevant items" and "about 5% of what I listed is probably spurious", and it knows when to stop searching.

label: v15V:v15:g1_mech
name: Self-Discovered Symmetry Group
anchor: evolving pool of composed answer-preserving transformations
mech: The system grows a pool of candidate input transformations by composing primitive edits (relabel, permute, reflect, rescale, swap roles). A candidate earns credit only if mapped-back answers agree under it more than they agree under random control edits of matched size, so a transformation that does nothing, or a model that ignores its input, earns no credit. Kept transformations must also close under composition: if T1 and T2 are kept, T1∘T2 must preserve answers too, and a failure of closure removes the weakest member. Answers that stay unchanged across the whole learned group become pseudo-labels for training and voting, and answers that break under it are flagged. The signal is the internal structure of the group, not verified cases.
value: The system discovers for itself which changes to an input must not change the answer, and uses that structure both to check its own answers without an oracle and to generalize far outside its training distribution.

label: v15V:v15:g2_imm
name: Schild Analysis Feature Surgery
mech: For cues that compete over an internal feature, the system titrates one cue against increasing amounts of the other and fits a Schild slope to the dose-ratio shifts. It also checks the pharmacological null-method invariant: a true single site gives the same antagonist affinity (pA2) whatever agonist cue is used. A slope away from 1, or a pA2 that depends on the agonist, triggers a split into gated sub-sites. The split is kept only if each new sub-site then passes both tests itself, so a mathematical invariant of the model's own activations grades the repair, not a fallible judge.
value: Features that are secretly several mechanisms are found and separated, and the result is checked by a quantitative law, so the model's internals become more faithful and reasoning that combines cues becomes more reliable.

label: v15V:v15:g1_loop
name: Surveyor's Hodge Network Adjustment
mech: Learned maps (analogies, translations, coordinate transforms) are composed around every independent cycle, and the misclosures are Hodge-decomposed. The gradient part is spread back over edges by least-squares network adjustment. The curl part is pinned to specific edges by a redundancy blunder test: an edge is condemned when the cycles that pass through it disagree with the cycles that avoid it. The harmonic part, which no local edit can remove, is treated as a real topological hole and gets a new context variable with separate charts and transition maps. Correctness comes from redundancy alone: a map is trusted in proportion to how many independent cycles close through it, as in surveying without a known benchmark.
value: The system can find out on its own whether a contradiction in its knowledge is an error to delete or a sign that it needs several context-dependent frames, and it builds those frames instead of averaging contradictory regularities into one incoherent map.

label: v15V:v15:g2_evo1
name: Staged Prequential Fact Quarantine
anchor: staged, delayed gating on disjoint ensemble subsets
mech: A new fact waits in a queue. At each stage, one disjoint subset of ensemble members provisionally absorbs it (treatment) and a matched subset does not (control). The fact's binding margin is how much better the treatment subset predicts the facts that arrive in the stream during the delay, measured before those facts are absorbed. The number of stages grows with how much of the model the fact would change, a fact with a negative margin at any stage is gone for good, and survivors are weighted by their accumulated margin. The world's later data, not the ensemble's opinion, grades each fact.
value: The system can keep learning from a stream of claims and admit only those that make it better at predicting what it encounters next, so wrong facts that would cause broad damage are stopped before they get in.

label: v15V:v15:g1_neg
name: Phase-Locked Event Clockwork
anchor: Kuramoto oscillator bank storing phase-locked patterns
mech: A bank of coupled phase oscillators runs continuously, timestamped events phase-reset or nudge it, and each oscillator adapts its natural frequency to reduce phase error at event onsets. Expectations are read out as the phase at which the next event should arrive. A phase-locking pattern is consolidated as a concept or routine only if its onset predictions on future events beat the same bank driven by jittered surrogate streams. The correctness signal is the actual arrival time of the next event, which the world supplies with no judge.
value: The system gets a real sense of duration, rhythm, deadlines and "something is late", and can discover hidden periodicities in event streams, which clockless token-sequence models cannot do.

label: v15V:v15:g1_core
name: Lock-In Concept Isolation
anchor: lock-in amplification with pseudo-random reference codes
mech: The system presents a few examples of a concept and matched non-examples in an order set by a pseudo-random reference code that it controls, and per-channel integrators multiply each internal activation by the code and low-pass the product. Several orthogonal decoy codes that drove nothing are demodulated at the same time, giving a measured noise floor and false-lock rate. Only channels locked above that floor form the concept's address. The address is re-tested with a fresh code and fading channels are dropped, so correctness rests on a causal fact the system knows for certain (what it varied), not on its own judgement.
value: Concepts can be isolated from very few noisy examples with a measured signal-to-noise ratio and false-detection rate, so the system knows how much to trust a concept it has just learned.
